definitions.definition: A declarative mathematical statement that is unambiguously either true or false.
A conditional statement formed by interchanging the hypothesis and conclusion of 'If P then Q' to get 'If Q then P'.
A specific instance or case that contradicts a proposition, proving a universal claim false.
An average where each data value is multiplied by a weight reflecting its size, count, or relative significance.

definitions.definition: A well-defined, finite, step-by-step computational procedure that takes inputs and produces outputs.
The largest positive integer that divides two or more integers cleanly without remainder.
A quadrilateral in which both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
The point where the three medians of a triangle intersect, representing its geometric center of mass.
An equation that can be written in the form ax + by + c = 0, where a, b, c are real numbers and a, b are not both zero.
The ratio of vertical change (rise) to horizontal change (run) between any two distinct points on the line.
The area of all curved outer surfaces of a 3D solid excluding flat base boundaries.

concepts.description: The truth value of a conditional proposition P -> Q is logically independent of its converse Q -> P. One can be true while the other is false.
A single valid counterexample is sufficient to disprove a universal claim, whereas verifying multiple positive examples does not constitute proof.

concepts.description: Taking a simple mean of group averages fails when sample sizes differ because it treats groups of unequal size as equal contributors.

concepts.description: Replacing iterative subtraction with division remainders reduces problem complexity from linear scale O(N) to logarithmic scale O(log N).
Connecting the midpoints of any quadrilateral always creates a parallelogram regardless of whether the original 4-gon is symmetric, skewed, or concave.
Any arbitrary quadrilateral can seamlessly tile a 2D plane because meeting 4 corners brings together all 4 interior angles summing to 360 degrees.
Every solution to ax + by + c = 0 corresponds to a point on a Cartesian line, and every point on the line is a solution (yielding infinitely many solutions).
The geometric relationship of two lines (intersecting, parallel, coincident) is governed entirely by the ratios of their algebraic coefficients.
For a fixed volume, a cube minimizes external surface area compared to elongated cuboids.

concepts.description: The volume of a sphere is exactly 2/3 of the volume of the circumscribing right circular cylinder of equal height and diameter.

properties.statement: Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.
In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal and opposite angles are equal.
A parallelogram is a rectangle if and only if its diagonals are equal in length.
A parallelogram is a rhombus if and only if its diagonals are perpendicular to each other.
The centroid G divides each median of a triangle in a 2:1 ratio from the vertex.
Lines intersect at a single point if and only if a1/a2 != b1/b2.
Lines are parallel (no solution) if and only if a1/a2 = b1/b2 != c1/c2.
Lines coincide (infinitely many solutions) if and only if a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2.

rules.rule_statement: If at least one counterexample x exists where P(x) is false, the universal statement 'For all x, P(x)' is false.
When merging groups with counts w_i and averages x_i, always sum total products (w_i * x_i) and divide by total sum of weights w_i.

rules.rule_statement: gcd(m, n) = gcd(n, m - n) for m >= n.
gcd(m, n) = gcd(n, m mod n) for m >= n.
The line segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and equal to half its length.
The volume of a cone is exactly 1/3 the volume of a cylinder with identical base radius and perpendicular height.

steps: 1. Identify the premise X and conclusion Y of proposition 'If X then Y'.
2. Search for a specific instance where premise X is satisfied.
3. Check whether conclusion Y fails in that instance.
4. If Y fails, state the instance as a valid counterexample disproving the proposition.
1. Identify distinct data groups x_i and their corresponding counts or weights w_i.
2. Multiply each group value x_i by its weight w_i to compute partial products.
3. Sum all partial products to get total weighted sum \sum (w_i * x_i).
4. Sum all weights to get total weight \sum w_i.
5. Divide total weighted sum by total weight.

steps: 1. Start with inputs m and n with m >= n.
2. Calculate remainder r = m mod n.
3. If r == 0, stop: n is the GCD.
4. If r > 0, set m = n and n = r, then repeat from Step 2.
1. Write both linear equations in standard form a1*x + b1*y + c1 = 0 and a2*x + b2*y + c2 = 0.
2. Calculate ratio fractions a1/a2, b1/b2, and c1/c2.
3. Compare a1/a2 and b1/b2: if not equal, conclude UNIQUE solution (intersecting lines).
4. If a1/a2 == b1/b2, compare with c1/c2: if not equal, conclude NO solution (parallel lines); if equal, conclude INFINITELY MANY solutions (coincident lines).
1. Multiply one or both linear equations by non-zero constants so coefficients of one variable become equal or opposite.
2. Add or subtract the equations to eliminate that variable.
3. Solve the resulting single-variable equation.
4. Substitute the solved value back into either original equation to find the second variable.

patterns.pattern_description: Positive integers with an odd number of distinct divisors are always perfect squares, whereas non-squares always have an even number of divisors.
Repeatedly subtracting the smaller integer from the larger integer preserves the exact set of common divisors.
Joining side midpoints of any 4-gon continuously generates parallelograms.
Plotting any number of solution pairs (x, y) for ax + by + c = 0 always yields points lying on a single straight line.
Scaling linear dimensions by k scales perimeter by k, surface area by k^2, and volume by k^3.
patterns.source: iemh206.pdf (Chapter 14: Math of Space: Surface Area and Volume)

problem_solving_strategies.methodology: To disprove a general statement, search systematically for a single valid case where premise holds but conclusion fails.
When combining non-uniform datasets, convert absolute counts into weights before taking arithmetic sums.
problem_solving_strategies.source: iemh202.pdf (Chapter 10: How Quantities Combine: Understanding Data)

problem_solving_strategies.methodology: Replace repetitive subtractive loops with integer remainder operations (m mod n) to accelerate computation.
Extend line segments or construct parallelograms to convert complex quadrilaterals into congruent triangles.
Check a1/a2, b1/b2, c1/c2 ratios prior to graphing or solving linear systems to immediately predict consistency.
Unfold 3D solids into 2D plane nets to calculate total surface area by summing planar face areas.
problem_solving_strategies.source: iemh206.pdf (Chapter 14: Math of Space: Surface Area and Volume)

problem_solving_strategies.methodology: Estimate massive global quantities (e.g. global water layer) by approximating total volume as Surface Area * thickness.
